reason: An appendage of the protonema is a part of it (e.g. a branch or bud), not the protonema itself. Reject, or use a part class if one exists.
Same as R3001: an appendage of the protonema is not the protonema.
Hydatode is a spelling variant of hydathode (water pore).
Hydatode is a spelling variant of hydathode.
Plural of hydathode.
A sinus is a leaf sinus only on a leaf or lamina. Basal sinus can also mean a sinus of a calyx or corolla.
Basal leaf sinus is the sinus at the base of the leaf blade, so it is a leaf sinus.
Gynostegial column is the gynostegium (Apocynaceae), the fused stamens and style head.
Gynostegium column is the gynostegium.

A resin pocket is a secretory cavity, but PO_0005656 'portion of secretory tissue' has gland as a synonym and is not a cavity. Use only where the existing rules already treat cavities as secretory tissue. Otherwise reject.
A resin cavity is a secretory space, not the tissue itself. Same doubt as R3010.
Plural of resin pocket, same doubt as R3010.
A sporangiaster is a sterile, sporangium-like structure of some fungi and ferns, not a spore-bearing sporangium. Mapping it to sporangium loses this meaning.
Plural of sporangiaster, same problem as R3013.
A modified sporangium is a special kind (e.g. a sporangiophore or a sterile type). The word 'modified' is lost. Reject.

The palea of a grass floret is a floret bract (a lemma-like part), not an inflorescence bract. The palea synonym in PO_0009054 is about the corn husk. Pistillate paleae are floret parts, so this is a doubtful target. Reject.
Same as R3016: palea is a floret part, not an inflorescence bract.
Same as R3016: paleae of florets are floret parts, not an inflorescence bract.
The leaves at the base of a pseudumbel are bracts of that inflorescence, so inflorescence bract fits only when the whole is the pseudumbel.
Pseudumbel leaf is an inflorescence bract only as part of the pseudumbel.
Plural of pseudumbel leaf, same reasoning.
A ray leaf may be a bract below a ray in a compound umbel (a bractlet). In other families a ray leaf is a leaf of a ray. Constrain it to umbels.
Leaf primordia is a listed synonym of vascular leaf primordium (plural).
A peristome filament is not a tooth. In some mosses the endostome has filaments (cilia, segments), which differ from the exostome teeth. Mapping all to tooth loses this.
Plural of peristome filament, same problem as R3024.
Filiform peristome teeth are peristome teeth. Filiform is a shape quality that should be split off.
The first leaf of a plant is a juvenile or seedling leaf only sometimes. In keys, 'first leaf' can also mean the lowest leaf of a shoot or inflorescence. The meaning depends on the context.
Première feuille has the same ambiguity as first leaf (seedling leaf or lowest leaf).
Premières feuilles has the same ambiguity as first leaf.
A glandular spot is a gland-dotted or colored patch on a surface. It is not a portion of secretory tissue. Handle as a spot with a gland quality, or reject.
Tache glanduleuse is a glandular spot or patch, same as R3030.
Tache glandulaire is a glandular spot or patch, same as R3030.
Plural of glandular spot, same as R3030.
The inner corona lobe is a distinct set of lobes in Apocynaceae and Passiflora. Mapping it to corona lobe loses inner. Only valid if no inner/outer contrast matters, so reject for now.
Inner is lost, as in R3034.
Inner is lost, as in R3034.
Coccus (coccum) is the one-seeded part of a schizocarp, such as in Euphorbiaceae. It is close to mericarp but not identical. 'coccu' looks like a truncated key, so check the match.
Involucellar bractlets form the involucel of Dipsacaceae, an epicalyx-like structure. They are not always epicalyx segments. Constrain to Dipsacaceae/Malvaceae contexts and check it by family.
Plural of involucellar bractlet, same doubt as R3038.
A floral shoot is not always the same as a reproductive shoot system. It is a rough match, but the flowering part is a branch or an axis in many floras.
Plural of floral shoot, same as R3040.
A flowering shoot is a shoot that bears flowers, which is a reproductive shoot system.
Pellucid dots are translucent dots seen in a leaf (oil glands in Rutaceae/Myrtaceae). Oil gland is a good guess for these families, but not for all taxa. Use a constraint on leaf, or reject.
Hypanthalamus does not exist as a word. It is likely a typo for hypanthium, so fix the typo upstream rather than adding a rule.
A leaf blade division can be a lobe, a segment, a leaflet or a pinna, so it is not always a lobe.
Plural of leaf blade division, same as R3045.
Divisions of the blade can be lobes, segments or leaflets, not only lobes.
A secondary pinna (second-order division) is the same as a pinnule only in a bipinnate frond or leaf. Check the order of division.
Plural of secondary pinna, same as R3048.

A throat appendage covers scales, folds or hairs in the throat of the corolla. The existing review already rejected 'corolla appendage' for the same reason, so only faucal scales in Boraginaceae would fit the corolline corona.
